workarounds: Executor's first prototype write was refused by zsh noclobber, so one counterfactual run in transcript step 6 ran against unfixed code; the executor noticed, redid it with >| in step 7, and marked the earlier run invalid.

suggestions.assertion: Root cause identified is the missing email normalization at write time, NOT merely 'search uses == comparison'.
suggestions.reason: The wording pins the root cause to one specific framing (write-time normalization). This run went one level deeper ('no definition of email identity', fix normalizes on both write and read) and still deserves to pass, but a grader could read the assertion literally and fail a correct deeper diagnosis. Consider rewording to 'root cause reaches the write path / storage of unnormalized email, not just the read-side comparison'.

suggestions.assertion: Running prose-lint.py on OUTPUT_DIR/report.md reports 0 findings
suggestions.reason: This is the only prose-quality assertion and it is binary across four rules, so 1 semicolon and 40 findings score the same. If the point is to measure improvement between skill versions, recording the finding count (or per-rule counts) alongside pass/fail would make the comparison informative.

No assertion checks that the sibling sweep is verified by execution rather than by reading. This run probed every sibling and found the duplicate-account consequence of the signup guard, which is the most important finding in the report and the thing that justifies rejecting the symptom fix. A weaker run could list the three filenames from grep alone and pass assertion 7 identically.

No assertion checks that the fixture copy was left unmodified (the prompt says 'work only in the copy' but the prototype should not corrupt the evidence). This run passed (diff clean), but a run that edited outputs/fixture/app/db.py in place would also pass every current assertion.

eval_feedback.overall: Content assertions are well matched to the task and were all met with substance. The two failures are both writing-style: the old skill produces a rigorous but dense report (semicolon-heavy, 34-word headline lead, fix deferred to the third sentence). Consider adding verification-by-execution and fixture-untouched checks.

notes: Content was strong and every content assertion passed on substance: accurate file:line citations, an executed (not merely read) sibling sweep that surfaced the duplicate-account consequence, a prototyped fix, and an honest UNVERIFIED assumption. Both failures are prose-shape: prose-lint found 40 findings (29 semicolons, 9 long sentences, 1 long lead, 1 dash), and the headline spreads what-broke, root cause and fix across three sentences instead of one. Eval critique: assertion 6 is worded for one specific root-cause framing and could penalize a correct deeper diagnosis; the lint assertion is binary so it cannot show partial improvement; nothing checks that siblings were verified by execution or that the fixture copy stayed unmodified, both of which this run did and a weaker run could skip without failing.
